title: The Gig Economy: Financial Challenges and Opportunities Faced by Freelancers
authors: Casalhay, S.F.; Guevarra, C.M.; Bragas, C.M.
venue: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
tldr: Qualitative study of Metro Manila freelancers reveals income volatility, limited access to benefits, and financial service barriers as primary challenges, with budgeting, emergency savings, and digital tools as common coping strategies.
problem_and_motivation: Freelancers in the gig economy face significant financial challenges including income volatility, lack of traditional employment benefits, and limited access to tailored financial services.
approach: Semi-structured interviews with 50 freelancers in Metro Manila across diverse fields.
Purposive and snowball sampling to ensure at least six months of gig work experience.
Use of NVivo software for coding and organizing themes.
findings: Income instability is the primary financial challenge, driven by seasonal fluctuations, client volume dependence, and unpredictable payments.
Freelancers lack traditional benefits such as health insurance, retirement plans, and paid leave.
Barriers to financial services include difficulty accessing loans, high interest rates, and documentation issues.
Financial tools like budgeting apps, digital wallets, and spreadsheets are widely used but have limitations.
Freelancers employ budgeting strategies including expense consciousness, structured allocation, and manual tracking.
Emergency fund saving and automated saving are common practices among freelancers.
Affordable health insurance tailored to freelancers would improve financial stability.
Policy and regulatory changes are needed to protect freelancers from non-payment and financial risks.
